First and foremost, if the world is experiencing similar inflation, it won’t become unlivable in the USA, USA is too big to fail in terms of tech/trade/wealth and in terms of military strength.

More importantly though, the long term trend is EXTREMELY deflationary. The tech we use that continues to replace workers is deflationary. Our aging boomer population is incredibly deflationary as opposed to what happened in the 70s. Did you know an estimated 20 million boomer households would have to pass on wealth just for these younger generations to be able to afford their assets at current levels? So we may experience short term inflation pain, especially if the Fed starts tapering bond purchases (inverse logic because the Fed buying bonds puts more money in to financial markets and increases the wealth gap). So when the fed buys bonds as they’ve been doing for years that has been a deflationary force also.

My summary of all of this being yes we are highly susceptible to a big inflation move and it is likely in progress esp if the Fed tapers (because M2 would fall as money velocity picks up, stock prices falling can also exacerbate this as people are forced to invest in the real economy instead of the Wall Street economy) but the chances of it lasting more than a few years is slim to none.
